input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Antoine Slim Shagreen Bedside Table
input.descriptionHtml:
In a Paris apartment the bedroom is often snug, and the table beside the bed has to earn its place: room for a lamp, a book and a glass of water, and nothing that crowds the way in and out. This bedside table is made for that kind of room. It is narrow and light on its feet, with an iron frame that keeps it airy, and its leather carries the pebbled grain of shagreen, the finish Paris case makers made fashionable in the eighteenth century.

The panels are leather embossed with that fine grain, a texture that is pleasant under the hand, set into the iron frame and finished with brass hardware. At 20 inches wide and 14 deep it fits beside a bed where a standard bedside table would be a squeeze, and at 34 lbs it is easy to lift when you rearrange the room. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it beside the bed in a guest room or a compact main bedroom with a slim lamp, a carafe and tonight's book, or use it in an entry as a small stand for keys and the mail. A pair also suits a narrow wall either side of a dresser. This listing is for one bedside table.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Honoré Shagreen Side Table
input.descriptionHtml:
On the Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the Paris street of the old leather and saddlery houses, fine leather is something you live with and touch every day rather than keep behind glass. This side table brings that habit home, made for the cup of coffee, the open book and the reading glasses set down beside a chair. Its top is covered in shagreen, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, so every small thing you put down lands softly on leather instead of bare wood.

The leather is wrapped over a wood frame, and a narrow trim of gold leather follows its edges, catching the light from a nearby lamp. It stands at a comfortable height beside a sofa arm or the side of an armchair, and it is heavy enough to stay put when someone brushes past on the way to the kitchen. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside a reading chair in a living room with a lamp, a short stack of books and a coaster for the evening drink, or use a pair at either end of a sofa. It also works beside the bed, with room for a clock and a glass of water. This listing is for one side table.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Émilion Two-Drawer Bedside Table — In Driftwood
input.descriptionHtml:
In Saint-Émilion the harvest ends with a long supper in the old town, and the walk home ends at the bedside with one last glass of wine and a book left open from the night before. This bedside table is made for the end of that walk home. Its top is broad enough for a lamp, the glass and the book together, and its two drawers keep everything else out of sight but within reach.

It is given a worn finish that looks as though it has seen many harvests already, with architectural detailing worked into its frame and hardware drawn for this piece alone. At 34 inches wide it gives more surface than most bedside tables, so it can also serve as a small chest in a hall or a guest room. It arrives fully assembled.

Set one on each side of the bed under a pair of lamps, or use a single one in a guest room with a carafe of water, a small clock and a few novels kept in the drawers for guests. This listing is for one bedside table.

Along the Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the leather houses have long been known for small things made with care: a case that closes neatly, a pocket for every item you carry. This side table brings that kind of order to the end of a sofa or the side of a bed, made for keeping the little things of the day within reach. Its three drawers hold the remotes, the reading glasses and the notebook, and its shagreen top, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, takes the cup set down beside them.

Shagreen leather covers the wood case, a slim trim of gold leather runs along its edges, and each drawer has a brass knob that is easy to find without looking. At only 20 inches wide it fits the gap beside a bed or a sofa where a bigger table would crowd the room. It arrives fully assembled.

Use it as a bedside table with a lamp, a glass of water and tomorrow's book on top and the small things of the night tucked inside, or set it at the end of a sofa where the drawers keep coasters and playing cards out of sight. This listing is for one side table.

In a family house off Clapham Common, mornings are a rush of school bags, lost socks and someone calling that there is no clean shirt, and the calm ones are the mornings when everything is where it should be. This small chest is made for that kind of calm. Its three drawers give each kind of folded thing its own place, and its top stays free for a lamp or a pile of clean laundry waiting to be put away.

It is made of tulip wood, a smooth, even-grained hardwood that takes a finish well, and at 26.5 inches wide and 16 deep it stands on very little floor. It arrives fully assembled, so it is ready to fill the day it comes.

Set it beside the bed in place of a bedside table, with a lamp, a clock and a photograph on top, or on a landing for towels and spare linens, or in a nursery where the top is a handy place to fold small clothes. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

Its tall posts and framed headboard make the bed feel like a room within the room, a quiet place to stay put a little longer while the light comes through the trees.

The headboard carries a pine veneer inside a softly crowned molding, and iron and brass details add a fine edge of metal. Standing 94 inches tall, it suits rooms with generous ceilings. It takes a king mattress and is delivered in three boxes, ready to assemble.

Give it pride of place in a main bedroom with high ceilings, dressed in crisp linen and a heavy quilt, with a bedside table at each side for a lamp and a morning cup. This listing is for one king bed, without mattress or bedding.

This box on a stand is made for keeping that kind of order at home. Its leather-covered box holds the papers and photographs you want safe but close, and it stands at side-table height, so the top still takes a lamp or a cup.

The box is wood covered in leather with an aged look, and inside it is lined with printed paper, so even a stack of old letters looks cared for when you open it. Brass accents and a neat line of nailheads finish the leather, and the whole box sits on a wooden stand. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside an armchair in a study or library, with a lamp and reading glasses on top and letters, passports and old photographs inside, or at the end of a sofa where it keeps the household papers out of sight. This listing is for one box on stand.

This bedside table brings that same sense of order to the end of the day. It pairs drawer space for small things with a door that closes over a deeper space, so the stack of books, the spare blanket and the water for the night all have somewhere to go.

It is made of pine with cast iron hardware and finished to look gently worn, and the detailing around the drawer and door gives it the presence of a much older piece. It is sized to stand beside a bed, and it works just as well at the end of a sofa or in a narrow hall. It arrives fully assembled.

Keep a lamp and a small dish for rings on top, reading glasses and a phone charger tucked out of sight, and an extra pillow or a folded throw behind the door. This listing is for one bedside table.

input.title: BH | Premier Roussillon Mango Pedestal Side Table — In Stone
input.descriptionHtml:
In Roussillon, the ochre village of the Luberon, mornings start slowly on a sunny terrace: a bowl of coffee, a book, and the light warming the red cliffs below. This pedestal table brings that slow start indoors. Its round top is wide enough for a coffee bowl, a plate of bread and an open book, and its single turned pedestal leaves room for your knees when you pull a chair up close.

It is mango wood in a natural finish, the pedestal turned on a lathe and rising to a round top 27 inches across. At 27 inches high it sits a little lower than a dining table, between a side table and a breakfast table, so it works as well beside an armchair as with a small chair drawn up to it. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Set it in a sunny window between two chairs with the coffee pot and the morning paper, or beside a reading chair with a lamp and a pile of paperbacks. This listing is for one pedestal table.

input.title: BH | Premier Klampenborg Round Side Table
input.descriptionHtml:
On the coast at Klampenborg, north of Copenhagen, the white houses Arne Jacobsen designed in the 1930s face the sea, and the light comes in off the water all afternoon: the kind of light made for a second cup of coffee and a conversation that wanders. This side table is made to sit right beside that conversation. Its round top keeps a cup within easy reach of whoever is talking, and its softly curved lines suit a bright room where every shape feels calm.

It is made of wood and shaped all the way around with smooth, rounded edges, so it reads as one soft form from every side of the room and feels as good under the hand as it looks. With no corners, it never catches a knee or a passing hip in a busy living room, and at 82 lbs it settles firmly wherever you place it.

Set it at the end of a sofa or between two armchairs by a window, holding a coffee cup, a small lamp and whatever book is being passed around. It also works on its own beside a reading chair in a bedroom. This listing is for one side table.

Its round marble top holds a reading lamp with room to spare for a book and a cup of tea, and at 29 inches tall it brings the light up level with the arm of a chair, right where the page needs it.

The base is iron with an aged finish, touched with brass at the details, and the top is marble with a softly aged surface, so the table looks as if it has stood in the same room for years. At 24 inches across it gives a lamp a steady footing without crowding a chair. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside a wing chair or at the end of a sofa with a lamp, a stack of novels and a small dish for reading glasses, or use a pair to flank a sofa in a drawing room. This listing is for one side table.

input.title: BH | Premier Wellfleet One-Drawer Side Table
input.descriptionHtml:
A Cape Cod cottage in Wellfleet keeps its evenings simple: a day on the bay, a swim before supper, and a paperback read by lamplight until the sea air wins. This side table is made for that last hour before sleep. Its top holds the lamp and the book, its drawer keeps the reading glasses and hand cream out of sight, and its open storage gives the next few books a place to wait.

input.descriptionHtml:
In the Regency villas of St John's Wood, the evening begins in the drawing room with a drink poured before dinner, and every good chair needs a small table close at hand for the glass. This side table is made for that hour. Its oval top sits neatly beside an armchair or at the end of a sofa with room for a glass, a small lamp and a dish of olives, and its antiqued gold accents catch the lamplight as the room grows dark.

It is made of pine, shaped in curving French lines and set with classical motifs, then finished to look gently aged. Its oval form has no sharp corners to catch a knee in a busy room, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside a wing chair by the fire with a decanter and a single glass, or at the end of a sofa holding a lamp, a coaster and the book you are halfway through. This listing is for one side table.

input.descriptionHtml:
In Panzano, a hill village in the Chianti Classico country south of Florence, lunch ends on the terrace with a last glass of red and a long view over the vines to the next hill. This side table is made for setting that glass down. At 28 inches tall it stands right beside a sofa or armchair, within easy reach of your hand, and its top is broad enough for a lamp, a bottle and two glasses together.

Its top is wider than it is deep, 32 inches across and 19 from front to back, so it runs along the side of a sofa without poking out into the walkway. It is finished to order, and at 41 lbs it is steady enough to stay where you put it while still easy to shift when the furniture moves around. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it at the end of a sofa with a reading lamp and a bowl of olives, or beside an armchair by a window where the afternoon light comes in. It works equally well beside a bed with a lamp and a book. This listing is for one side table.

input.title: BH | Premier Chenonceau King Bed — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
At Chenonceau the château stands on arches across the river Cher, and in the morning the light comes up off the water and through the windows of its long gallery. Waking slowly to that kind of light is the whole idea of this bed. Its headboard gives you somewhere to sit up with the first coffee of the day, and its footboard posts frame the bed so it feels settled and complete from across the room.

The frame is solid beech with acacia veneer, a thin layer of acacia laid over the surface to show its warm, lively grain. The footboard posts stand 33 inches tall, and the bed rides 6 inches off the floor, so the frame looks light and the floor beneath stays easy to clean. It takes a king mattress and needs assembly.

Make it the heart of a main bedroom, with linen sheets, a lamp and a carafe of water on a table at each side, and a window left uncurtained for the morning. This listing is for one king bed, without mattress or bedding.

In the Providence Athenaeum, the old subscription library where Poe courted the poet Sarah Helen Whitman in 1848, readers drift between tall cases, taking down one volume and then another. This bookcase brings that habit of browsing home. Its arched glass doors let you see every spine before you open them, and four shelves give a growing collection room to spread out, from paperbacks to the books you keep for life.

It is built of reclaimed pine, wood given a second life, so the grain carries the marks of its first one. At 91 inches tall it fills a wall with presence while staying only 18 inches deep. The doors keep dust off the books while leaving every title on show, and it arrives fully assembled.

Stand it in a library, study or living room, with first editions and favourite novels behind the glass, a few framed photographs and pieces of pottery between the rows, and a reading chair close by. This listing is for one bookcase.

Set it along a wall in a study or behind a sofa that floats in the room, with favourite books inside and a bowl, a small sculpture and a stack of auction catalogues on top. This listing is for one bookcase.

Horace Walpole built Strawberry Hill in the mid-1700s as a Gothic fantasy beside the Thames, and its library, with bookcases set within pointed arches, was where he read and wrote through long evenings. This console is made for keeping books close to where you read. Its open shelves put the spines in easy view at sofa height, and a four-lobed motif borrowed from Gothic tracery runs along its sides and back, a small nod to that library.

It is made from reclaimed pine in a distressed finish, so the old grain shows through, and the edges of its top and shelves are carefully detailed. At more than six feet long it holds a good row of books with room for a few objects between them. It arrives fully assembled.

Run it behind a sofa that faces into the room, or along a hall or study wall, with books on the shelves and a pair of lamps, a bowl and a framed print on top. This listing is for one console table.

It is built of pine and pine veneer and stands more than seven feet tall on a footprint just 36 inches wide and 19 deep, so it offers a great deal of display space while taking very little floor. Stand it in a dining room for serving bowls and the good glasses, in a living room for books and pottery, or at the end of a hallway with a lamp or a small sculpture at eye level. This listing is for one display cabinet.

Set it on the wall facing the sofa in a family room or den, with the screen on top, a basket of blankets beside it and a framed print or two hung above. This listing is for one media cabinet.

In the Marais, the old quarter of Paris, tea is still taken properly: a pot brewed with care, two good cups, a plate of small cakes, and an hour set aside simply to talk. This tea table is made for that kind of afternoon for two. Its round pine top takes the pot, the cups and a plate of cake, and at 30 inches high it suits a pair of chairs pulled in close, so the conversation stays close as well.

This side table is made to hold that first glass. Its glass top catches the low sun the way the village's own glass does, and its iron base, forged by hand, holds it steady beside a low chair.

The top is cast glass, poured into a mould rather than cut from a sheet, which gives it a soft depth at the edge, and the base is forged iron in an aged brass finish. It is the larger of two sizes in this design, so it can stand alone or sit beside its smaller partner. It comes in two boxes and needs assembly.

Place it beside an armchair or at the end of a sofa with a lamp and something cold to drink, or group it with the smaller table in front of a window seat. This listing is for one side table.

On the café terraces around the Maison Carrée, the Roman temple at the heart of Nîmes, the afternoon is measured in glasses of rosé set down on small marble-topped tables. This table brings that terrace hour indoors. Its round marble top is cool and smooth under a glass, with room for a carafe, two glasses and a plate of olives, and its iron base swells into full, generous curves that give a small table real presence.

The top is marble, with the soft veining of natural stone, and the base is iron in an aged finish that has the look of a café table well used. At 32 inches across and 28 inches high it sits between a side table and a small bistro table, ready to serve either way. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Set it in a small foyer with a vase of flowers and a bowl for keys, or in a sunroom corner with two chairs drawn up for an afternoon glass and a game of cards. This listing is for one side table.

Keep it beside a reading chair or tucked in at a sofa's end, holding a cocktail, a small dish of salted almonds and a book left face down at the page you stopped on. A pair works well too, one at each side of a sofa, so nobody has to reach across to set a glass down. This listing is for one side table.

It sits on an iron stand shaped to look like bamboo, a style much loved by Victorian collectors, and at 25 inches tall it doubles as a small side table. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside an armchair or at the end of a sofa, with a cup of tea and a lamp on the lid and the remotes, coasters and a deck of cards inside. This listing is for one box on a stand.

input.descriptionHtml:
For centuries Fleet Street was London's street of newspapers, where reporters wrote and filed their copy wherever they could find a surface and a few quiet minutes. This table is made for that kind of writing on the move, around the house. At 27 inches tall it brings a laptop up to an easy typing height beside an armchair or the end of a sofa, so the email you have been putting off gets written right where you sit.

Its top is leather over MDF, a dense engineered board, edged all around with a row of brass nailheads, and it stands on an iron base in an antiqued brass finish. At 24 lbs it is light enough to carry from the living room to the bedroom, and it arrives fully assembled.

Keep it beside a reading chair or a sofa arm with a laptop, a notebook and a cup of coffee, or by the bed for the morning papers. This listing is for one laptop table.
